summary.text: A 10-year-old female with no menstruation or history of sexual life was admitted with lower abdominal pain for over three weeks and vaginal bleeding lasting more than two weeks. Intermittent right lower abdominal pain with occasional diarrhea began three weeks before admission and fever of 38.6°C four days before admission subsided with antipyretic treatment. A local ultrasound one week before admission showed a pelvic mass, and serum hCG exceeded 297,475 IU/L, prompting referral.

On examination vital signs were stable with no palpable lymphadenopathy or significant tenderness. Laboratory tests showed hCG 282,995 IU/L, elevated C-reactive protein 54.2 mg/L, hemoglobin 93 g/L and slightly elevated total thyroxine 192.72 nmol/L. Ultrasound with Doppler and contrast-enhanced CT showed a large heterogeneous hypervascular pelvic mass with central necrosis, chest CT showed right lung nodular opacities suggestive of metastases, and cranial CT showed no intracranial abnormality.

She underwent exploratory laparotomy with removal of the right adnexa, extensive omentectomy and retroperitoneal lymph node sampling, which showed a 12 cm solid mass with dense adhesions. The pathological diagnosis was non-gestational ovarian choriocarcinoma of the right ovary, with strong CD146, CK18, HCG and HPL positivity, Ki-67 above 90%, and negative P63, SMA and EMA.

article_limitations: Single index patient; the literature-review and general discussion statements are not patient facts. The source lists no tables or supplements.
No calendar dates are given; times are relative to admission only where the sentence states them, and no outcome after surgery or follow-up is reported.
Disease extent and stage are not stated; lung lesions are described as radiologically suggestive of metastasis in the case text but as identified metastases in the discussion.
Hyperthyroidism and normal tumor markers are mentioned only in the discussion as consistent with this case; the underlying results are not reported.
Serum hCG appears as >297,000 IU/L (abstract), >297,475 IU/L (referral) and 282,995 IU/L (laboratory tests); the abstract value is kept review_only as a probable rounded duplicate.
